headline: Self-talk is your inner voice—the running commentary that shapes how you see yourself and life
universal_truth: You talk to yourself more than anyone else talks to you; make sure it's helpful
fun_facts: The average person has 12,000 to 60,000 thoughts per day—most are self-talk
Negative self-talk correlates with anxiety, depression, and lower performance
Athletes who train positive self-talk perform better under pressure
discussion_questions: What does your inner voice typically say?
Is your self-talk mostly supportive or critical?
How does your self-talk affect your actions?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: There's a voice in your head. It narrates, judges, plans, worries. You've heard it so long you might not notice it. But what it says shapes everything—your mood, your actions, your life. What is your inner voice saying?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Does self-talk really matter? It's just thoughts—private, invisible, seemingly harmless.

options.text: Self-talk shapes reality—you believe what you repeatedly tell yourself; critical self-talk becomes self-fulfilling prophecy; supportive self-talk builds confidence and resilience
options.response: Yes. You're with yourself constantly. That inner voice influences every moment. If it's harsh, life feels hard. If it's supportive, challenges feel manageable. The voice matters enormously.
True, but thoughts precede actions; what you tell yourself affects what you do...

q1.title: Noticing the Voice
q1.script: First step: notice what you're saying to yourself. Most self-talk is automatic and invisible. Pause and listen. What tone does your inner voice use? What does it typically say?
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Noticing the Voice"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Friend or Critic
q2.script: Would you talk to a friend the way you talk to yourself? Often our inner voice is harsher than we'd ever be to others. Notice if you're being cruel to yourself in ways you'd never be to someone else.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Editing the Voice
q3.script: You can change self-talk. Not instantly, but with practice. Catch harsh statements. Replace them with what you'd say to a friend. This rewiring takes time but transforms internal experience.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You talk to yourself more than anyone else talks to you. Make sure it's helpful. Be a good companion to yourself.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 349. Tomorrow, we'll explore words that shape beliefs—affirmations. Until then, listen to your inner voice.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Self-Talk Audit - What Are You Saying?
growTrack.learning_objective: Become aware of and improve self-talk
growTrack.activity: For one day, notice your self-talk. What do you say when you make a mistake? When you succeed? Is the voice supportive or critical? Practice catching one harsh statement and replacing it with what you'd say to a friend.
